topic: Roblox color, contrast, and non-color state communication guidance

claims.claim: Roblox officially recommends sufficient contrast between text and its background and specifically warns against light text on light backgrounds and dark text on dark backgrounds.
claims.scope: In-experience Roblox UI text and backgrounds; qualitative accessibility guidance.
limitations: The Roblox page gives no contrast-ratio formula or numeric minimum.
This is platform guidance, not an engine-enforced requirement.
The examples establish the direction of the guidance but do not define a conformance test.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines — Color contrast
sources.supports: Roblox says players may struggle with light-on-light or dark-on-dark text and recommends text/background colors with sufficient color contrast.

sources.title: Cross-platform development — Accessibility
sources.supports: Roblox says all text should be legible on all screens and all UI should have sufficient contrast.

claims.claim: The WCAG 2.2 Level AA thresholds are 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large-scale text; these are imported external web-accessibility thresholds, not Roblox engine requirements.
claims.scope: W3C WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.3 for web content; usable as an external design target for Roblox UI only when a project intentionally adopts it.
limitations: Roblox Creator Hub's current color-contrast section does not state, incorporate, or enforce these ratios.

WCAG defines large-scale text in web typography terms, including 18 pt regular or 14 pt bold in its explanatory material; direct conversion to Roblox TextSize is not established by the cited Roblox sources.
Inactive UI components, incidental text, and logotypes have exceptions under WCAG SC 1.4.3.
A computed ratio must not be rounded up to pass a threshold.
No evidence was found that the Roblox engine automatically evaluates these ratios.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)
sources.supports: External W3C guidance states at least 4.5:1 for text and images of text, with at least 3:1 for large-scale text, and documents the exceptions and threshold handling.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines — Color contrast
sources.supports: The current Roblox source recommends only 'sufficient color contrast' and supplies no numeric ratio, establishing that the WCAG numbers should not be relabeled as Roblox requirements.

claims.claim: WCAG 2.2 Level AA uses a 3:1 threshold for visual information needed to identify active UI components and states, and for meaningful graphical objects; this is also an imported external threshold rather than a Roblox requirement.
claims.scope: W3C WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.11 for web content; potentially adoptable as an external design target for active Roblox controls and meaningful graphics.
limitations: Inactive UI components are excluded by WCAG SC 1.4.11.
The criterion applies to visual information required to identify a component or state, not necessarily every pixel, border, decoration, or state-to-state color pair.
Roblox's cited guidance does not state this 3:1 minimum or claim engine enforcement.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
sources.supports: External W3C guidance requires at least 3:1 against adjacent colors for visual information required to identify active UI components, their states, and meaningful graphical objects, with exceptions.

sources.title: Cross-platform development — Accessibility
sources.supports: Roblox provides only the qualitative instruction that UI have sufficient contrast; it does not supply the WCAG non-text ratio.

claims.claim: Roblox officially advises creators not to rely on color alone to communicate information, actions, or outcomes for players with color-vision deficiencies, and recommends pairing color with non-color cues such as symbols, icons, shapes, or patterns.
claims.scope: Gameplay and in-experience UI distinctions that communicate meaning to sighted players, including players with color blindness.
limitations: The general accessibility page specifically demonstrates symbols alongside color; the UI curriculum also mentions icons, shapes, and animations.
Roblox does not prescribe one universal alternate cue for every state.
An animation-only alternate may introduce separate motion-accessibility considerations; the cited color sections do not resolve that interaction.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines — Color non-reliance
sources.supports: Roblox uses a grayscale example and recommends different symbols alongside colors so more players can distinguish gameplay and other information.

sources.title: Cross-platform development — Accessibility
sources.supports: Roblox says nothing should rely solely on color to distinguish an action or outcome.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Select a color theme
sources.supports: Roblox recommends combining colors with icons, shapes, and/or animations instead of always relying on color alone, specifically for colorblind players.

claims.claim: The external WCAG rule likewise prohibits using color as the only visual means of conveying information or state; a hue-only status distinction is therefore insufficient under that web standard.
claims.scope: W3C WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.1 for web content; separate from Roblox-specific guidance, although directionally consistent with it.
limitations: WCAG explains that a luminance difference of at least 3:1 can count as an additional visual distinction in some cases, but not when users must identify the particular color itself, such as green-valid versus red-invalid.
This WCAG rule must not be presented as a Roblox engine requirement.
Roblox independently publishes similar qualitative guidance, so WCAG is corroboration and a separable external standard rather than the sole basis for the Roblox recommendation.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.1: Use of Color
sources.supports: External W3C guidance says color must not be the only visual means of conveying information, indicating action, prompting a response, or distinguishing an element, and explains the hue-versus-lightness nuance.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines — Color non-reliance
sources.supports: Roblox independently recommends symbols alongside colors, showing aligned Roblox-specific guidance without importing WCAG's numeric details.

claims.claim: For on-screen text that may overlay a changing 3D scene, Roblox recommends placing text on a contrasting color or giving it a stroke so it does not blend into the background.
claims.scope: In-experience UI text, especially screen overlays with potentially variable underlying 3D content.
limitations: Roblox presents a contrasting backing surface and a text stroke as alternatives, not as a rule that every text element must have both.
The source gives no required stroke thickness, stroke opacity, or numeric contrast ratio.
The recommendation is about legibility; it is not an engine rendering guarantee that a stroke will succeed against every possible scene.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Determine a text system
sources.supports: Roblox identifies the possible underlying background behind on-screen text and recommends displaying text on a contrasting color or with a stroke when background noise would reduce legibility.

claims.claim: Roblox recommends a limited color theme whose colors maintain consistent, quickly learned associations with UI functions, but does not publish a universal semantic mapping such as red always meaning error or green always meaning success.
claims.scope: Color semantics within an individual Roblox experience and its genre conventions.
limitations: The tutorial's bright-color/selectable and green-plus/health examples are illustrative and contextual, not mandatory platform tokens.
The source recommends consistency and limited key associations but does not define named semantic roles or fixed RGB values.
Genre conventions may affect appropriate associations, so the guidance is not a universal palette specification.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Select a color theme
sources.supports: Roblox defines a color theme as colors that each communicate a message through consistent application, gives bright color as a selectable-state example, and recommends limiting the palette to key functional associations.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Identify your UI elements
sources.supports: Roblox discusses categorizing UI by purpose and making semantic design choices; green and/or plus icons for health are presented as an example rather than a platform-wide rule.

claims.claim: Roblox recommends that overlay UI colors remain readable over both light and dark elements in the 3D world.
claims.scope: Screen-space UI composited over variable in-experience 3D imagery.
limitations: This guidance concerns robustness against changing scene luminance; it does not require a separate user-selectable dark theme and light theme.
The sample uses black and white neutral colors for most overlay UI, but that sample choice is not a universal mandatory palette.
No numeric worst-case contrast test is specified.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Select a color theme
sources.supports: Roblox says to prioritize simple UI with color readable over both light and dark elements in the 3D world, and explains that the sample uses black and white overlays against a colorful 3D environment.

claims.claim: An official Roblox requirement that every in-experience UI provide separate dark and light surface themes was not found in the reviewed Creator Hub accessibility, cross-platform, UI-art-style, and styling sources.
claims.scope: User-selectable light/dark theming for creator-built, in-experience UI.
limitations: Roblox's platform applications or Studio may have their own themes; that does not establish a requirement for creator-built in-experience UI.
The official guidance instead addresses sufficient contrast, readability over both light and dark world content, and the player's preferred background transparency.
Absence is limited to the current official sources reviewed and the Context7/web-search queries recorded for this assignment.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines
sources.supports: The current Roblox accessibility page covers contrast and player preferences but does not prescribe dual light/dark experience themes.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Select a color theme
sources.supports: The current Roblox design curriculum requires readability over light and dark 3D content but does not turn that into a dual-theme requirement.

claims.claim: Roblox officially recommends respecting the player's Preferred Transparency setting so UI backgrounds become more opaque when the player requests it, improving readability and contrast.
claims.scope: In-experience GUI backgrounds with transparency; player accessibility preference exposed through GuiService.PreferredTransparency.
limitations: This is about background opacity, not a numeric foreground/background contrast guarantee.
The documented implementation multiplies each element's authored BackgroundTransparency by PreferredTransparency; creators must identify and apply it to relevant UI elements.
It does not replace testing color contrast across scene and device conditions.

sources.title: Accessibility guidelines — Preferred transparency
sources.supports: Roblox states that PreferredTransparency of 0 indicates a preference for fully opaque backgrounds for readability and contrast and recommends multiplying BackgroundTransparency by this value.

claims.claim: Roblox provides an engine-level non-interactable GUI state that can be targeted by UI state styling: when GuiObject.Interactable is false, its GuiState is NonInteractable, and Roblox style state selectors correspond to GuiState values.
claims.scope: Roblox GuiObject interaction state and StyleRule state selectors.
limitations: This establishes a state and styling hook, not a prescribed disabled appearance.
The cited API does not say that setting Interactable=false automatically greys, fades, or desaturates an element.
GuiObject.Active has different input/event semantics and should not be treated as identical to Interactable based on these sources.

sources.title: GuiObject.Interactable and GuiObject.GuiState
sources.supports: The official API states that Interactable controls whether the GuiObject can be interacted with and that false keeps GuiState at NonInteractable.

sources.title: GuiState enum
sources.supports: The official enum lists NonInteractable as the state in which the GUI cannot be interacted with.

sources.title: CSS Comparisons — Pseudo-classes
sources.supports: Roblox documents state selectors as the styling equivalent of CSS pseudo-classes and ties them to GuiState values.

claims.claim: No official Roblox visual-design rule was found that disabled controls must use a fixed opacity, desaturation amount, grey palette, or reduced-contrast treatment.
claims.scope: Appearance of disabled/non-interactable controls in creator-built Roblox UI.
limitations: Roblox exposes NonInteractable as an engine state, so creators can style it, but the reviewed official sources do not prescribe how.
The UI curriculum recommends visual feedback for interactable elements, but its examples concern focus/interaction feedback and do not define a disabled-state recipe.
A project may adopt its own accessible disabled-state tokens, but that would be a project design recommendation rather than an official Roblox requirement.

sources.title: GuiObject.Interactable
sources.supports: The API defines the functional NonInteractable state without specifying opacity, desaturation, grey, or contrast values.

sources.title: Choose an art style — Establish an interaction order
sources.supports: Roblox recommends at least one form of visual feedback for interactable UI and gives outline, size, color, or animation examples, but does not prescribe disabled-state treatment.

claims.claim: WCAG 2.2 exempts inactive UI components from its minimum text and non-text contrast criteria; this external exception does not require or recommend making disabled Roblox controls low contrast.
claims.scope: W3C WCAG 2.2 web-content conformance, not Roblox engine behavior or Roblox-specific visual styling.
limitations: The exception means the cited WCAG success criteria impose no minimum on inactive controls; it is permission, not a design instruction.
A disabled control still needs to be understandable in its product context, but no Roblox-specific numeric or visual treatment was found.
This exception must not be generalized into a Roblox rule that disabled elements should be faint, grey, or invisible.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) — Inactive User Interface Components
sources.supports: External W3C guidance says text that is part of an inactive UI component has no SC 1.4.3 contrast requirement and illustrates, rather than mandates, a low-contrast disabled browser button.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.11: Non-text Contrast
sources.supports: External W3C guidance excludes inactive UI components from the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement.

conflicts: Roblox's current official contrast guidance is qualitative ('sufficient contrast'), while WCAG supplies numeric 4.5:1 and 3:1 thresholds. The numeric thresholds are compatible external targets but are not Roblox engine requirements or stated Roblox minima.

Roblox exposes NonInteractable as an engine state but gives no official disabled appearance. WCAG's inactive-component contrast exception removes a web-conformance minimum; it does not fill that design gap or mandate low-contrast disabled styling.
Roblox's green-plus/health and bright-color/selectable examples illustrate contextual semantic associations. Treating them as universal Roblox meanings would overstate the source.
Roblox's instruction to remain readable over light and dark 3D content is not the same as requiring separate light-mode and dark-mode surface themes.
unresolved: No official Roblox numeric contrast threshold, contrast-calculation method, or engine enforcement mechanism was found in the current sources.
No official Roblox opacity, desaturation, greyscale, or contrast prescription for disabled controls was found.
No official Roblox requirement for separate user-selectable light and dark themes in creator-built in-experience UI was found.

Context7-first resolution selected /websites/create_roblox and returned relevant Roblox material for contrast, color non-reliance, strokes, semantic color associations, light/dark 3D backgrounds, and NonInteractable state. Context7 did not supply prescriptive Roblox material for disabled appearance or separate experience themes, so direct current Creator Hub retrieval and web-search fallback were used; no such official prescription was verified. The Firecrawl CLI was unavailable in this environment, so the fallback used the available direct URL reader and web search.
